correctness.rationale: For odd u,v, h=(u^2+v^2)/2 is 1 modulo 4. The 2-adic square-root lemma produces lambda with lambda^2=2/h-1 modulo 2^(k+1); both explicit half-sum vectors are integral and have norm 1 modulo 2^k. Their sum is (u,v). Adding a coordinate basis norm-one vector proves exact 3C and 4C parity coverage. The modulo-eight square classification excludes (2,2) from 2C for k>=3, and moduli 2 and 4 are checked separately. The standalone verifier replayed exact sumsets for k=1..7 and all 87,381 constructive odd-odd instances through k=9. Finite experiments support rather than prove the all-exponent claim.

value.rationale: The canonical dyadic Gaussian norm-one subgroup has a natural, nontrivial additive Cayley graph. The finding determines its exact diameter over all prime-power exponents, exhibits the sharp transition after exponent 2, and proves full parity-coset coverage at exact lengths 3 and 4 via a structural 2-adic square-root lemma; the local obstruction at modulus 8 forces diameter 4. It is a complete invariant, not a finite arbitrarily chosen slice or a routine direct residue check.
